title: Agpeya Opening
text: O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our God. O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our King. O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our Saviour.

meta.source: CORRECTED 2026-08-18: previous text was unsourced (did not match any wording in the Coptic Agpeya). Replaced with the real opening of O'Leary 1911's Morning Office item (2), p. 88, public domain.

title: Theotokion
text: O Mother of the True Light, we glorify thee as the Mother of God, for thou hast borne for us the Savior of all.

meta.status: FLAGGED 2026-08-18: sourcing unverified, not yet checked against O'Leary or any other primary source. Left unchanged pending Phase 2 of the Coptic Agpeya rebuild (the Theotokia weekly cycle), when this should be replaced with real sourced content or removed.

title: Prayer Recited After Each Office
text: Lord, have mercy upon us. Lord, have mercy upon us. Lord, have mercy upon us. O Holy Trinity, our God, have mercy upon us. Have mercy on the work of thy hands and save our souls.

meta.source: De Lacy O'Leary, The Daily Office and Theotokia of the Coptic Church (London: Simpkin, Marshall, Hamilton, Kent & Co., 1911), p. 87 -- 'Prayers recited after each Office.' Public domain.

title: Prayer of Thanksgiving
text:
Let us give thanks to the benevolent and merciful God, the Father of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. For he has shielded us, helped us, kept us, purchased us to himself, spared us, assisted us, and brought us to this hour. Therefore let us pray him that he the Almighty Lord our God may keep us this holy day and all the days of our life in peace.

O Master, Lord God Almighty, Father of our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ, we give thanks to thee concerning everything, and for everything, and in everything, for thou hast shielded us, helped us, kept us, purchased us to thyself, spared us, assisted us, and brought us to this hour. Wherefore we pray and beseech thy goodness, O Lover of men, grant us to pass this holy day and all the days of our life in all peace and in thy fear. Take away from us and from all thy people and from this holy place all hatred, all temptation, every operation of Satan, the counsel of wicked men and the uprising of enemies concealed or manifest. But do thou vouchsafe to give us those things which are expedient or needful. For thou art he who hast given us power to tread upon serpents and scorpions and all the might of the enemy. And lead us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil, by the grace and mercy and love for men of thy only-begotten Son, our Lord and God and Saviour Jesus Christ, through whom be glory and honour and power and worship due to thee, and to him, and to the Holy Ghost the Life-giver consubstantial with thee; now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (1), pp. 87-88. Public domain.

title: O Come, Let Us Worship
text:
O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our God. O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our King. O come let us worship, come let us pray to Christ our Saviour.

Our Lord Jesus Christ, Word of God, our God, through the intercessions of the Holy Mary and all thy saints, keep us and let us glorify thy good glory, and have mercy on us according to thy favour, for ever.

The night has passed, we thank thee, O Lord, and we pray thee to keep us this day without sin and deliver us.

And on his son Jesus Christ, the Word who became flesh: he died and rose on the third day; he hath raised us with him. One Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is the same in Its substance: proceeding from the Father It has hallowed all creation. It teaches us to worship the Holy Trinity in one Godhead and one nature. We praise and bless thee for ever. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (2), pp. 88-89. Public domain. A lesson from Ephesians 4:1-6 is appointed at the marked point in the source and is resolved separately from this component (see the rubric's reading slot).

title: We Glorify the Trinity
text:
We glorify Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, the Holy and Consubstantial Trinity; hail Church, house of the angels. Hail Virgin who didst bear our Saviour; hail Gabriel who broughtest good news to her. Hail Michael the Archangel, hail Raphael the truth divider, hail Souriel and all the angels, ye four beasts without body; hail ye four and twenty elders. Hail Cherubim, hail Seraphim; hail all ye host of heaven. Hail John the great forerunner; hail ye twelve Apostles. Hail Father Mark the Evangelist, destroyer of idols. Hail Stephen the first martyr; hail George the morning star. Hail all ye choir of martyrs; hail Abbot Antony and ye three Abbots Macarius. Hail all ye choir of cross-bearers; hail ye saints who have pleased the Lord.

Through their prayers, O Christ our King, have mercy on us in thy kingdom.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (4), pp. 89-90. Public domain.

title: O True Light
text:
O true light which enlightens every man coming into the world. Thou didst enter the world through thy love for men; all creation rejoiced at thy coming. Thou didst save Adam from deceit, thou didst deliver Eve from the pains of death. Thou didst give us the spirit of adoption; we praise and bless thee with thy angels.

When the hour of morning comes to us, O Christ our God the true Light, may thoughts of light abound in us, and may not the darkness of passion overcloud us. So that we may praise thee reasonably with David as we cry aloud and say: "My eyes have prevented the hour of dawn in meditating on all thy sayings. Hear my voice according to thy great mercy; save me, O Lord my God, according to thy loving-kindness."

O God, who dost regard the well-disposed, who providest for thy elect: strong guide of those who take refuge in thee, who desirest the safety and deliverance of every creature; in thy Christliness thou hast prepared for us the night; grant us this day to be without sin, that we may be worthy to lift up our hands to thee in thy sight, without anger or evil thought. Order our goings in and our goings out this morning in the joy of thy protection; that we may speak of thy righteousness every day and praise thy power with the prophet David: "In thy peace, O Christ our Saviour, we have slept and arisen and trusted in thee."

Behold the excellence, behold the pleasantness that brethren dwell together in unity. They sound together in true love evangelical, after the Apostles. Like the ointment on the head of Christ, that ran down upon his head even to his feet. It anointeth every day, old and young, and youths and servants. These the Holy Ghost has joined together like a harp; they praise God always in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, day and night with heart unwearied.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (5), pp. 90-91. Public domain. Includes O'Leary's translation of Psalm 119:147-148 and Psalm 4:8 as woven into the hymn text.

title: Doxology of the Virgin
text: Thou art the mother of the Light, the holy mother of God; thou didst contain the unconfined Word. After that thou didst conceive him thou didst remain still a virgin; in songs and praises we exalt thee. He in his favour with the good will of his Father and of the Holy Spirit came and saved us. We ourselves pray that we may obtain mercy through thy intercessions to him the Lover of men.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(i), p. 91. Public domain.

title: Doxology of the Angels
text: Thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand archangels and holy angels are standing before the throne of the Almighty; they sing and say: "Holy, holy, holy in truth, glory and honour are due to the Trinity." Through the intercessions of the choir of angels, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(ii), p. 91. Public domain.

title: Doxology of the Apostles
text: Our fathers the Apostles preached amongst the Gentiles about the gospel of Jesus Christ. Their sound went out over all the earth, their words reached to the ends of the world. Our Saviour chose the Twelve, he gave them commandment, and thus he said: "Go ye not into the way of the Gentiles, nor to the city of the Samaritans; but go ye rather after the lost sheep of the house of Israel. Heal those that are sick; freely have ye received, freely give." He said "among the Gentiles" because it was for our father to go there with the Holy Spirit. Through the prayers of our lords and fathers the Apostles, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(iii), pp. 91-92. Public domain. Includes O'Leary's translation of Matthew 10:5-8.

title: Doxology of the Martyrs
text: Crowns unfading hath the Lord placed upon all the choir of the martyrs. He preserved them and granted that they should find refuge in him, and be with him in his kingdom. Through the prayers of the choir of martyrs, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(iv), p. 92. Public domain.

title: Doxology of Abbot Antonius
text: Blessed be thy name, great Abbot Antonius, it has been glorious in all the land of Egypt. It shines forth in the heart of the faithful like the beams which convey the light of the sun. Thou art the tree bearing fruit sevenfold, according to the word of the prophet. Thou didst bring us good news of life eternal and of good things which eye hath not seen; let us invoke the name of our Lord Jesus, according to the precepts of the great Abbot Antonius; and let us ask the goodness of the Father that he bestow on us the fire of the Holy Spirit. May it burn vehemently, consuming our souls, and may it purge a temple for the Holy Trinity. Through the prayers of the great Abbot Antonius, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(v), p. 92. Public domain.

title: Doxology of Abbot Paul
text: Thou art blessed, O Father Abbot Paul, for thou didst complete thy course well. Thou didst love solitude like Elias, thou wast in the desert like John. Thou didst overcome the powers of the adversary and extinguish the arrows of the evil one. Thou didst climb the steps of the virtues, thou didst become a citizen within the heavens. Thou didst win the crown of righteousness, thy name went forth to all places. Through the prayers of the righteous Abbot Paul, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(vi), pp. 92-93. Public domain.

title: Doxology of Abbot Macarius
text: To thee only did the God of heaven give great joy, O Abbot Macarius. Thou didst show the way to many souls until thou didst conduct them to Jerusalem in heaven. O God, who wast with our righteous father the great Abbot Macarius, be with us. Through the prayers of the three abbots Macarius, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(vii), p. 93. Public domain.

title: Doxology of the Cross-Bearers
text: Thy saints bless thee, they relate the glory of thy kingdom. Thy kingdom, O God, is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion is to all generations. Our holy fathers went into the desert, they ate the fruits beneath the trees. The angel of the Lord came to them every Sabbath and every Lord's Day. He consoled them, and strengthened and fortified the beloved brethren. "I will lay aside your bodies and not cast them out amidst the reptiles and wild beasts, but I will wrap them for burial, for these are bodies which have been pleasing to God." They loved seclusion, they had recourse to the desert that they might reach the purity of angels. Those few brethren were despised; they hoped to attain eternal life. Through the prayers of the choir of cross-bearers, O Lord grant to us the pardon of our sins.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(viii), p. 93. Public domain. 'Cross-bearers' here denotes Confessors, per O'Leary's own note.

title: Doxology of the Patriarchs and Prophets
text: Hail Elias the wise prophet, and Eliseos his listening disciple. Great was the report in the land of Egypt of Mark the Apostle, its first guide. O Mary the Virgin, thou art the mother of God, pray to Him for us that he may be merciful to our race. O great Patriarch, Abbot Severus, who gave forth holy doctrine to enlighten our minds; our Father the Confessor, Abbot Dioscorus, contended for the faith against heretics. And all our Fathers who pleased the Lord; may their holy praise be to us a protection. Through their prayers may God grant to us pardon for our sins and give us salvation.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (6)(ix), p. 94. Public domain.

title: The Angelic Song
text:
Let us sing with the angels, Glory to God in the highest, and in earth peace, and good will to men. We praise thee, we bless thee, we glorify thee, we confess thee, we declare thy glory, we give thanks to thee because of the greatness of thy glory, O Lord King over heaven; O God the Father Almighty, O Lord the only-begotten Son Jesus Christ, and the Holy Spirit. Lord God, Lamb of God, Son of the Father, who takest away the sins of the world, have mercy upon us: who takest away the sins of the world, receive our prayer. Who sittest at the right hand of the Father, have mercy upon us. Thou alone art holy, thou alone art exalted, Lord Jesus Christ, with the Holy Spirit. Glory to God the Father. Amen.

I will praise thee every day, I will praise thy holy name for ever and ever. Amen. Very early in the morning does my soul arise to thee, O Lord; for thy commandments are lights upon earth. I have meditated on thy ways, for thou art a help. Early in the morning, O Lord, dost thou hear my voice. My morning prayer is to thee, that thou look upon me.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (7), pp. 94-95. Public domain.

title: The Trisagion
text:
Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, who wast born of the Virgin, have mercy upon us.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, who wast crucified for us, have mercy upon us.

Holy God, Holy Mighty, Holy Immortal, who didst rise from the dead and ascend to the heavens, have mercy upon us.

Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Holy Trinity have mercy upon us. All-Holy Trinity have mercy upon us. Holy Trinity have mercy upon us. O Lord, pardon our sins. O Lord, pardon our transgressions. O Lord, pardon our offences. O Lord, help those who are sick amongst thy people: heal them for the sake of thy holy name. Remember the souls of our fathers and brethren who have pleased the Lord. Kind Lord, have mercy upon us; kind Lord, help us; accept our prayers. For thine is the glory and power and threefold holiness. Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Lord, have mercy. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (8), p. 95. Public domain. This is the expanded 'Trisagion with the additions' distinctive to Coptic (non-Chalcedonian) use, not the plain Byzantine Trisagion already elsewhere in this app -- kept as its own distinct component rather than reusing ecu-trisagion.

title: The Creed
text:
We believe in one God the Father Almighty, who made heaven and earth, and all things visible and invisible.

We believe in one Lord Jesus Christ, only-begotten Son of God, begotten of the Father before all ages. Light of Light; True God of True God; Begotten, not made; Consubstantial with the Father, by whom all things were made. Who for us men and for our salvation came down from heaven, and became flesh of the Holy Spirit and of the Virgin Mary, and was made man. He was crucified for us under Pontius Pilate; he suffered and was buried. He rose from the dead on the third day according to the Scriptures. He ascended into the heavens; he sits at the right hand of the Father, and shall come again in his glory to judge the living and the dead; of whose kingdom there is no end.

And we believe in the Holy Ghost, the Lord and Life-giver, who proceedeth from the Father; who with the Father and the Son is worshipped and glorified, who spake by the prophets. In one holy Catholic and Apostolic Church. We confess one baptism for the remission of sins. We look for the resurrection of the dead, and the life of the world to come. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (10), pp. 95-96. Public domain. Given here as its own component (cop-creed) rather than reusing the app's existing comm-creed-* components, since Coptic use omits the Filioque clause ('who proceedeth from the Father' only, with no 'and the Son').

title: The Forty-One-Fold Kyrie
text: Lord, have mercy. (Repeated forty-one times, in commemoration of the thirty-nine lashes of Christ's scourging, the crown of thorns, and the spear in his side.)

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (11), p. 96: 'Kyrie eleison forty-one times.' Public domain. The traditional count-explanation given in the rendered text is standard Coptic devotional teaching, not O'Leary's own wording, since he gives only the rubric.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe)
text: O Master, Lord God of hosts, who art from everlasting and endurest for ever, who made the sun for a light of the day, and established the night for rest for all flesh. We thank thee that thou hast caused us to pass this night in peace, and hast brought us to the beginning of the day. Therefore we pray thee, O King eternal, that the light of truth may shine upon us and illuminate us with the light of thy divine knowledge, and make us children of the light, children of the day; that we may pass this day in purity and truth, in good order, and that we may pass the rest of our life blameless. By the grace and the love towards man of thy only-begotten Son, and the gift of the Holy Spirit; both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Morning Office item (12), pp. 96-97. Public domain.

title: Troparion of the Third Hour
text:
Thy Holy Spirit, O Lord, which thou didst send upon thy Holy Disciples and Blessed Apostles at the third hour, do thou not take from us, O Good One, but let It be renewed within us.

Thy Holy Spirit, O Lord, which thou didst send upon thy Holy Disciples and Blessed Apostles at the third hour. A clean heart create within me, O God, and renew a right spirit within me.

Thy Holy Spirit, O Lord, which thou didst send upon thy Holy Disciples and Blessed Apostles at the third hour. Cast us not from thy presence, nor take thy Holy Spirit from us.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

O Lord, who didst send thy Holy Spirit upon thy Holy Disciples and thy Blessed Apostles at the third hour, take it not from us, O Good One, but we pray thee let It be renewed in our inward parts, O Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, the Word. A right and quickening Spirit, a prophetic and pure Spirit, a sanctifying and governing Spirit, upon everything. For thou dost give light to our souls; thou who dost enlighten every man who cometh into the world, have mercy on us.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O Mother of God, thou art the true vine-tree, for thou didst bear the grapes of life. To thee we pray, thou full of grace, and to the Apostles, on account of the salvation of our souls. Blessed be the Lord our God, blessed be the Lord daily. May the God of our salvation make our way prosperous to us.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Third Hour item (2), pp. 97-98. Public domain. Weaves in O'Leary's translation of Psalm 51:10-11 ('A clean heart create within me...', 'Cast us not from thy presence...').

title: Second Troparion of the Third Hour
text:
O heavenly King and Paraclete, Spirit of Truth, who art in every place and fillest all. O treasure of good things and giver of life. Graciously come and be within us, purge away every sin, O thou Good One, and save our souls.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

As thou wast in the midst of thy disciples, O Saviour, and didst give them peace, be with us and save us.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Whenever we stand in thy holy temple, we consider ourselves as those who stand in heaven. O Mother of God, gate of heaven, open to us the door of mercy.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Third Hour item (5), p. 98. Public domain.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe) of the Third Hour
text: O God of every mercy and of all comfort, who hast comforted us at all places and all times. We thank thee that thou hast raised us up to pray at this holy hour, when thou didst pour out the grace of thy Holy Spirit abundantly upon thy Holy Disciples and Blessed Apostles. We pray and beseech thee, O Lover of men, accept our prayer, and send down upon us spiritual benediction, in order that we may walk in the spirit and not fulfil the lusts of the flesh. By the power of thy only-begotten Son Jesus Christ our Lord, through whom be glory and honour and power and worship due to thee, and to him, and to the Holy Ghost the Life-giver consubstantial with thee; now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Third Hour item (7), p. 98. Public domain. O'Leary's own printed text ends '...who, &c.' -- his shorthand for a doxology conclusion he does not spell out again at this specific point. CORRECTED 2026-08-18 per governance rule (no abbreviated/placeholder liturgical text): completed using the doxology O'Leary himself gives in full at the end of the Morning Office's Prayer of Thanksgiving (cop-mp-thanksgiving) -- 'through whom be glory and honour and power...consubstantial with thee; now and always and for ever and ever. Amen.' Confirmed via independent cross-check against several other English editions of this same traditional prayer (contemporary, copyrighted, not quoted here) that this is in fact the standard formula this prayer concludes with -- not a guess, and no new wording invented; only O'Leary's own already-transcribed translation reused.

title: Troparion of the Sixth Hour
text:
O thou who on the sixth day and at the sixth hour wast nailed to the cross on account of the sin which Adam dared in paradise. Take away the handwriting of our sins, O Christ our God, and save us.

O thou who on the sixth day and at the sixth hour wast nailed to the cross on account of the sin which Adam dared in paradise. But I have called upon God and the Lord hath heard me. O God, hear my prayer, and turn not thy face from me and hear me.

O thou who on the sixth day and at the sixth hour wast nailed to the cross on account of the sin which Adam dared in paradise. At even and at morn and at noon will I utter my words and he will hear my voice, he will save my soul in peace.

O thou who on the sixth day and at the sixth hour wast nailed to the cross on account of the sin which Adam dared in paradise.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

O Jesus Christ our God, who wast nailed to the cross at the sixth hour, thou hast destroyed sin by the wood and hast given life to the dead by thy death, to man whom thou didst make by thy hands and who died by sin. Destroy our passions by thy sufferings and by the nails wherewith thou wast nailed. Purge our minds from evil, in our works and lusts, in accordance with thy pity.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

As we have no excuse by reason of the multitude of our sins, through thee, O Mother of God, we have access to him whom thou didst bear. Great is thy intercession, mighty and acceptable to our Saviour. O pure Mother, cast not out us sinners from thy intercessions to him whom thou didst bear. For he is merciful and mighty towards us, for he suffered on our account that he might save us. Let thy mercies come quickly to us, for we are greatly in need. Help us, O God our Saviour. For the glory of thy name, O Lord, save us. Forgive us our sins for the sake of thy holy name.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Sixth Hour item (2), pp. 99-100. Public domain. O'Leary prints the refrain once ('O thou who...') then abbreviates its repetitions as 'O thou who, &c.' before each different paired verse of Psalm liv (=55) -- resolved here per the no-placeholder governance rule by writing the refrain out in full before each of its three appearances, exactly as O'Leary's own rubric indicates it is to be repeated. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' likewise resolved to their standard full forms.

title: Second Troparion of the Sixth Hour
text:
Thou hast caused salvation in the midst of the earth, O Christ our God; by stretching forth thy hands upon the cross. Therefore all nations cry aloud, Glory to thee, O Lord.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

We adore thine incorrupt form, O Good One; we ask for forgiveness of our sins, O Christ our God. For thou didst consent in thy good will to ascend the cross, that thou mightest deliver from bondage to the enemy those whom thou didst make. We cry to thee, we give thee thanks. Thou hast filled all with joy, O Saviour, thou who didst come to help the world. To thee, O Lord, be glory.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Sixth Hour item (5), p. 100. Public domain. No separate Theotokion follows this troparion in O'Leary's text -- the source moves directly to item (6), the 41-fold Kyrie.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe) of the Sixth Hour
text: We thank thee, O our Lord, the Almighty, Father of our Lord, God and Saviour, Jesus Christ, and we glorify thee. For thou hast ordained the hours of the passion of thy only-begotten Son to be times of prayer and supplication. Accept our prayers, and blot out the handwriting of our sins written against us, even as thou hast broken it down during these holy hours, upon the cross of thy only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Lord, and Saviour of our souls, by whom thou hast dissipated all the might of the adversary, and hast given us a season of light and pure life and peaceful being, that we may praise thy name, holy and reverend; and may stand before the dread and just tribunal of thy only-begotten Son, Jesus Christ our Lord; and with the saints may glorify thee, the Father without beginning, and the Son consubstantial with thee, and the Holy Ghost the giver of life, now and always and unto all ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Sixth Hour item (7), pp. 100-101. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: Troparion of the Ninth Hour
text:
O thou who didst taste death in the flesh at the ninth hour for our sakes, destroy our bodily lusts, O Christ our God, and save us.

Let my cry come before thee, O Lord; give me understanding, O Lord, according to thy word.

O thou who didst taste death in the flesh at the ninth hour for our sakes, destroy our bodily lusts, O Christ our God, and save us.

Let my prayer come before thee according to thy word and quicken me.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

O thou who didst give up the spirit to the hands of the Father, who didst hang upon the cross at the ninth hour: who didst lead into paradise the thief who hung beside thee, forget me not, O Good One, nor cast me off, but purge my soul and illuminate my understanding. And bestow upon me the favour of thy immortal mysteries. So that when I have tasted thy loving-kindness I may offer to thee song unending. I long for thy beauty above everything, O Christ our God, and do thou save us.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O thou who wast born for us of the Virgin, and didst bear the Cross, thou Good One. By thy death thou didst slay death and didst show forth thy resurrection. O God, reject not those whom thou hast made by thy hand; show forth thy love for man, O Good One; and accept the prayers of thy Mother for us. O our Saviour, save the lowly people; cast us not away for ever, nor leave us; do not revoke thy promise. From us remove not thy mercies, for the sake of thy friend Abraham, thy servant Isaac, and thy holy one Israel.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Ninth Hour item (2), pp. 101-102. Public domain. O'Leary directs the refrain to be said again with '(repeated)' rather than reprinting it -- resolved here per the no-placeholder governance rule by writing the refrain out in full both times. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' likewise resolved to their standard full forms. The two verses paired with the refrain ('Let my cry come before thee...', 'Let my prayer come before thee...') are O'Leary's own full translation of Psalm 119:169-170, given by him in full at this point -- no resolution needed for those.

title: Second Troparion of the Ninth Hour
text:
When the thief saw the Author of Life hung upon the cross, he said: If he who is now crucified with us were not a god in the flesh, the sun would not have become dark nor would earth be shaken and quake.

O thou who hast power in all things, and who holdest all, do thou be mindful of me, O Lord, when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

O thou who didst receive the confession of the thief upon the cross; purchase us to thyself, O Good One, though we have incurred death by our sins. We acknowledge our sins with him, we confess thy Deity. With him we cry to thee: Remember us, O Lord, when thou comest into thy kingdom.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

When the Mother saw the Lamb, the Shepherd and Saviour of the world hanging upon the cross, weeping she said: The world indeed rejoices, it receives salvation. My bowels are inflamed, I behold thy hanging, thou who hast suffered for all, my Son and my God.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Ninth Hour item (5), p. 102. Public domain.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe) of the Ninth Hour
text: O God, Father of our Lord God and Saviour, Jesus Christ: who by his appearing has redeemed us and delivered us from the bondage of the adversary: in his blessed and great name we pray thee turn away our minds from the cares of life and the desires of the world to the recollection of thy heavenly judgements. In us complete thy love to man, O Good One; and let the prayer of the ninth hour be always acceptable in thy sight. Grant that we may walk worthy of the calling whereunto thou dost call us, so that when we go forth from the body we may be reckoned amongst the true worshippers of the passion of thy only-begotten Son our Lord Jesus Christ; and may receive mercy and pardon of our sins and salvation and the dwelling of the saints who have done thy will in truth from all eternity. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Ninth Hour item (7), pp. 102-103. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: Troparion of the Eleventh Hour
text:
I have sinned before thee, O Lord, like the lost son. But receive me, O Father, who repent: O God, have mercy upon me.

To thee, O Lord, I lift up mine eyes, who dwellest in the heavens. Behold, as the eyes of servants are upon the hands of their masters, and as the eyes of a maid-servant upon the hands of her mistress; even so our eyes are upon thee, O Lord God, until thou have mercy on us.

Early will I call thee, O Lord my Saviour, with the voice of the publican, saying: O God, forgive me as him, and have mercy upon me.

Have mercy on us, O Lord, have mercy on us. We have been full of reproach, and our soul is filled exceedingly. Make the reproach for the wealthy, and make the reproach for the proud.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

The athletes who desire not the pleasure of earth have thereby become fit for the pleasure of heaven, and are made fellows with the angels. Through their intercessions, O Lord, deliver us and have mercy upon us.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O Mother of God, preserve the flock from all troubles; we all have recourse to thee after God. Like a strong wall be to us a defence.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Eleventh Hour item (2), pp. 103-104. Public domain. The middle section ('To thee, O Lord, I lift up mine eyes...') is O'Leary's own full quotation of Psalm 123:1-2 -- given here as printed, verbatim from O'Leary rather than swapped for a corpus lookup, since it is presented as part of the troparion's continuous prose, not as a separately-headed reading. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their standard full forms per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Vouchsafe, O Lord
text:
Be graciously pleased, O Lord, to grant us that we may be this day without sin. Blessed be thou, Lord God of our fathers. Blessed be thy greatness. May thy holy name be filled with glory for ever. Amen.

May thy mercy come upon us, O Lord, as we have trusted in thee. For the eyes of all look to thee, for thou dost give them meat in due season. Hear us, God our Saviour, the help of the ends of the earth, and do thou vouchsafe to save us in this generation and for ever. Amen.

Blessed be thou, O Lord: teach me thy truth. Blessed be thou, O Lord: enlighten me with thy truth. O Lord thy mercy is for ever. Cast not the works of thy hands from thee, O Lord, for thou hast been to us a place of refuge from the beginning for ever.

I have said, Lord have mercy on me; save my soul, for I have sinned against thee. O Lord, I flee to thee; save me, teach me, make me turn to thee, for thou art our God.

May the fountain of life open under thee; in thy mercy, O Lord, let us see mercy. May thy mercy come to those who know thee, and thy truth to those who are right in heart.

Praise befits thee, song befits thee, glory is due to thee, Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, who were from the beginning, and are now, and for ever and ever. Amen.

We declare, O Lord, the praise of thy exalted name, the proclamation of thy mercy by day, and thy truth by night.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Eleventh Hour item (3), pp. 104-105. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself -- no abbreviation to resolve. Weaves in several psalm-verse echoes (Psalms 33, 25, 86, 36, and others) as part of O'Leary's own continuous translation, not as separately cited readings.

title: Second Troparion of the Eleventh Hour
text:
Hail thou who hast found grace, Holy Mary, Mother of God: blessed art thou amongst women, and blessed is the Fruit of thy womb. Thou hast borne to us the Saviour of our souls.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

Holy John, who baptized Christ, remember our congregations, that we may be set free from our misdeeds. Thou hast received favour to intercede for us.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

Our holy Fathers, the great Abba Antony, the three Abbots Macarius, our Father Abba John, our Father Abba Pishoi, our Father Abba Pakhom, our Father Abba Theodore, and our righteous Father the great Abba Samuel: Intercede for us, that we may be delivered from trouble and distress: we have you as intercessors before Christ.

O Mother of God, we have recourse to the protection of thy mercies: Despise not our prayers in need, but save us from destruction, O thou alone blessed.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Eleventh Hour item (6), p. 105. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their standard full forms.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe) of the Eleventh Hour
text: We thank thee, O Lord the Merciful; for thou hast permitted us to pass this day in peace and brought us to the evening with thanksgiving, and hast allowed us to see the evening light. Receive, O God, our praise made now, and save us from the snares of the adversary, and defeat all his wiles against us. Graciously grant us this coming night peace without trouble or distress or phantasm, that we may spend it in peace and purity; that we may offer to thee hymns and prayers always and in all places. In all things we glorify thy name with the Father the Unconfined, without beginning; and the Holy Ghost, the giver of life, consubstantial with thee now and always and for all eternity. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Eleventh Hour item (8), pp. 105-106. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: Prayer of Esaias
text:
God is with us.

Know this, all ye Gentiles, that God is with us.

Know this unto the ends of the earth, that God is with us.

All ye that devise shall be defeated, and if ye have again made strong your hands, ye shall be made feeble, for God is with us.

And every counsel that ye make shall not stand, for God is with us.

All that ye say shall be made void, for God is with us.

We fear not your terror, nor are we dismayed in heart, for God is with us.

But the Lord, him will we praise, for he is our God, he is our strength, for God is with us.

We have trusted in him, because of him we shall be saved, for God is with us.

Behold, I and the children given me by God, people that walked in darkness, have seen a great light: and they that dwelt in the land and shadow of death, on them hath the light shined, for God is with us.

Unto us a Child is born; unto us a Son is given, for God is with us.

The government shall be upon his shoulder, he is a mighty Counsellor, for God is with us.

Thy Mighty God, the Ruler, for God is with us.

The Prince of Peace and Father of the world to come, for God is with us.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Twelfth Hour item (2), pp. 106-107. Public domain. Woven throughout with O'Leary's own translation of Isaiah 8:8-10 and 9:6.

title: Troparion of the Twelfth Hour
text:
Behold, the day is passed; we thank thee, O Lord, and pray thee graciously to grant us this evening and this night to be without sin. O Saviour, protect us.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

Behold, the day is passed.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

The immaterial creatures, the Cherubim, full of eyes, and the Seraphim with six wings, with unceasing cry magnify thee, together with the angels, in the hymn "Thrice holy before the world, thou the Father without beginning, and the Son consubstantial with thee, and the Holy Ghost the giver of life, Trinity undivided". Thou hast appeared to us by means of the holy Virgin, through thy Word, that is Christ our Helper. Thou hast called the Athletes and Prophets and Martyrs to everlasting life through thyself, and they assembled pray for the pardon of our offences, because we have turned away from striving through the deceit of the adversary. Deliver us and we shall praise thee with the Angels, saying, "Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of Sabaoth, heaven and earth are full of thy glory."

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Twelfth Hour item (3), p. 107. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.', 'Both now, &c.', and the refrain repetition ('Behold, the day is passed.') resolved to their full forms per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Litany of the Twelfth Hour
text:
Thou holy Mother of God, intercede for us sinners.

Ye powers of heaven, Angels and Archangels, Cherubim and Seraphim, intercede for us sinners.

Saint John, Forerunner, Baptist and Martyr, intercede for us sinners.

Holy Apostles, Preachers and Evangelists, intercede for us sinners.

All Prophets working signs, Moses and Aaron, Elias and Eliseos, and all the other prophets, intercede for us sinners.

All ye choir of Martyrs, Confessors, and holy Athletes, intercede for us sinners.

Our holy Fathers, the High Priests who strove for the orthodox faith, intercede for us sinners.

Our holy Fathers, the cross-bearers, bearers of the Spirit, who forsook the world, intercede for us sinners.

Through the incomprehensible power of the holy Cross remove not thy mercies from us.

Lord, forgive me a sinner, and have mercy on me, for blessed art thou unto eternity. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Twelfth Hour item (5), p. 107. Public domain. O'Leary abbreviates each intercession line after the first as '...intercede, &c.' -- resolved here per the no-placeholder governance rule by writing out 'intercede for us sinners' in full on every line, exactly as the opening line establishes.

title: Second Troparion of the Twelfth Hour
text:
Thou Lord, who knowest the watching of my enemies and understandest the weakness of my nature, O Creator, behold I commit my spirit into thy hands. Protect me under thy good wings, that I sleep not in death. Open my eyes to the greatness of thy works; raise me up always to praise thee. Thou only art the Good One and Lover of man.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

Dreadful in thy judgement, O Lord, when men assemble and the Angels stand round. Then the books will be opened and deeds will be revealed, and recollections will confess. What decree will be pronounced on me who am bound in sin? Who will quench the flaming fire for me? Who will give light to my darkness, unless thou have mercy on me, O God? Thou art the One who showest mercy to men.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O Mother of God, since we trusted in thee we shall not be ashamed, but since we have received help and intercession, O holy, pure, and perfect one, we do not fear; we shall put to flight our foes and disperse them. We take refuge with thee as a shield in all things. We pray and beseech that we may invoke thee, Mother of God, so that thou rescue us by thy prayers. Do thou raise us again from the oblivion of sleep that we may give praise through the power of the God who took flesh in thee.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Twelfth Hour item (9), pp. 107-109. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their full forms per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Concluding Prayer (Metremhe) of the Twelfth Hour
text: O Master, Lord Jesus Christ our God, grant to us rest in sleep, rest for our bodies and cleanness for our souls; protect us from that darkness which is the shadow of sin. May the movements of lust be quiet, may the swelling of the flesh be stilled: grant us a watching mind and humble recollection, behaviour full of virtue, a bed undefiled and a couch that is clean. Do thou make us to arise for the Night and Morning Praises, and grant us praise throughout the night, that we may bless thy holy name, full of glory and all beauty, with thy good Father and the Holy Ghost the giver of life, now and ever and for all eternity. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Prayer of the Twelfth Hour item (11), p. 109. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: Beginning of the Midnight Office
text:
Arise and be the children of the light. Let us sing to the Lord of hosts, that he vouchsafe to us salvation from our sins. Whilst we stand before thee in body remove from our mind the sleep of ignorance. Grant us, O Lord, to be children of the bride-chamber, that we may be wise and stand before thee at the hour of prayer. And that we may offer thee the praise which is seemly, and may obtain remission of our sins which are many. Glory to thee, O Lover of men.

"Behold now praise the Lord, ye servants of the Lord. Ye who stand in the courts of the house of our God. In the night lift up your hands to the sanctuary: bless the Lord."

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

"The Lord bless thee out of Sion, who made heaven and earth."

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (1), p. 110. Public domain. O'Leary notes this is a choir or Deacon's portion found in almost all copies of the Psalmodia. 'Glory be, &c.' resolved to full form (twice) per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Doxology After the Psalm
text: Glory to thee, good Lover of men. Glory to thy virgin Mother and all thy saints. Glory to thee, Lover of men. Glory to thee, only-begotten. Holy Trinity, have mercy upon us.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (2), p. 110. Public domain. Said after Psalm 119, following the Gloria Patri (given in Greek, then Coptic, in the manuscript -- O'Leary does not translate the Gloria Patri itself here since it is the same universal doxology already given in full elsewhere in this app, e.g. within cop-mo-opening).

title: Let God Arise
text: Let God arise and all his enemies be scattered. Let every creature that hates his Holy Name flee before him. But let thy people be in blessings, thousands of times and ten thousands of times. Let them all do thy will. O Lord thou dost open my lips, and my mouth showeth forth thy praise.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office, p. 111 (unnumbered, between items (2) and (3)). Public domain. Draws on O'Leary's translation of Psalm 68:1-3 and Psalm 51:15.

title: Troparion of the First Nocturn
text:
Behold the bridegroom cometh in the middle of the night. Blessed the servant whom he findeth waking. But he whom he findeth sleeping is not ready to go with him. See, my soul, that thou art not heavy with sleep, lest thou find thyself outside the kingdom. But watch and cry Holy, Holy, Holy, art thou, O God. For the sake of the mother of God have mercy on us.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

O my soul consider the dread day, and await the bridegroom and light thy lamp with the oil of joy, for behold the bridegroom. See, my soul, that thou do not sleep, lest thou find thyself outside the door, like the five foolish virgins. But keep the watch of prayer, so as to meet the Lord Christ with rich oil, and may he grant thee the true marriage of his deity.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O Virgin Mother, impregnable fortress, defeat the devices of the adversaries and turn thy servants' trouble of heart to joy. Be the defence of our city, and contend for our kings and intercede for the peace of the world. For thou art our help, O Mother of God.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (3), p. 111. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their full forms per the no-placeholder governance rule. The closing Theotokion is O'Leary's own note (n.1): a Greek Theotokion following this Troparion in the Greek office.

title: Troparion of the Second Nocturn
text:
Grant to me, Lord, fountains of many tears, as thou didst grant long ago to the woman who was a sinner; and make me worthy to wash thy feet which have made freedom in place of the way of error. And I will bring to thee ointment of sweet savour; and I shall secure a pure life through penitence, so that I may hear the voice full of great joy, "thy faith hath made thee whole."

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

When I contemplate the multitude of my evil deeds, and there enters into my heart the memory of that fearful judgement, trembling seizes upon me. I will flee to thee, O God, thou Lover of man. Turn not away thy face from me, I pray thee, for thou alone art without sin. Vouchsafe to my unhappy soul a right fear before the end come and save me.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

The heavens praise thee, thou full of grace, thou unwedded bride. And we ourselves glorify thy unspeakable child-bearing. O Mother of God, intercede for the salvation of our souls.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (9), p. 112. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their full forms. The closing Theotokion is O'Leary's own note (n.1): the Greek Theotokion following this Troparion.

title: Troparion of the Third Nocturn
text:
Look, O Lord, with an eye of pity upon my distress, for my life has almost come to an end, and in my works is no safety. Wherefore I pray thee that with an eye of mercy, O Lord, thou look upon my littleness and save me.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

As though the Judge were before thee watch, O my soul, and await the bridegroom. And consider the dread hour, for in judgement there is none who will have pity. Wherefore forgive me, O my Saviour, for thou alone art the Lover of men.

Both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

O gate of reasonable life, noble Mother of God, save them from troubles who have recourse to thee with faith: that we may glorify thy holy child-bearing in everything, for the salvation of our souls.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (11), pp. 112-113. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' and 'Both now, &c.' resolved to their full forms.

title: Prayer
text: Remember, O Lord, all the saints who have pleased thee from the beginning, and grant to me also that I may lay aside everything that does not please thy goodness. I know in truth that thou wouldest that I should not be a sinner, but I myself do evil by the will that is in me. Grant me, O Lord, that I may reject evil works and my numerous sins; in order that I may find mercy for the rest of my life, as long as I am in this dwelling-place: and when thou biddest me come forth from the body I may present myself before thee without confusion, and may find mercy and confidence with thee, in thy judgement which is faithful and full of glory. For thou art God of mercy, and blessing is due to thee always, henceforth and for ever. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (13), p. 113. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: Prayer of S. Simeon Stylites
text:
O Lord, grant me a prayer without error, with recollection of my thoughts; in order that I may ask in faith in thy promises which thou hast vouchsafed to me. Grant me power of seeing in my thoughts and mind. May my heart receive light so that my intelligence may grasp that which is pure, that I may hear thy eternal mysteries, the things which thou hast prepared for the human race by the grace of Christ. Concede to me, O Lord, a pure heart, that I may pray to thee uninterruptedly. O Master, remove my thoughts from deeds which are contrary to nature, that I may give thanks with understanding for the grace of thy mercy, and that I may give thanks with ready understanding for the good things which thou hast promised to me: things which eye hath not seen nor ear heard, nor have they entered into the heart of man, which thou hast made ready for them that love thy holy name. Give me, O Lord, the love of thy Holy Spirit that may impel my intelligence so that I may love thee with all my heart and all my soul, and all my strength as thou hast told me. And the love of my neighbour even as myself; this is the fulfilment of the law and the prophet. Grant me to control my thoughts so that I may regard nothing save thee; nor ever pray to thee with my lips alone whilst my attention is astray, that evil comes into the innermost part of my heart. For it is written that my light and salvation is the Lord. O my Lord God, draw me towards thee, for thou art the true God and One that has pity and compassion, and that teachest good things, and a Righteous King. For thou art my treasure-house and treasury, and my precious stone and crown of my praise. For thou in truth art my bridegroom, and my paradise and my tree of life. Thou dost put round me my armour and my might and strength and readiness in words. For I am without heart and portion upon earth. But thou art he who pities every creature which thou hast created and made from that which was not. And thy pity directs our race into thy kingdom. And I myself, O Lord, may I love thee as is fitting, and do not thou reject the promises thou didst promise to me through thy Christ, that there may not anything in my life prevent my eyes and my heart, but let them see them as the plants of the earth. By the power and the mercy of thy only-begotten Son and the gifts of thy Holy Spirit.

Now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (14), pp. 113-115. Public domain. 'Now, &c.' resolved to its full form per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Prayer (Repeated Three Times)
text:
I glorify thee, O Lord Jesus Christ the merciful, and I pray thy goodness, O Lover of men, have mercy upon me according to thy great kindness, and forgive all my sins, and vouchsafe to me a pure repentance and deliver me from every sin to death.

(Said three times.)

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (15), p. 115: 'The following prayer is repeated three times.' Public domain. The repetition instruction is retained as a plain rubric note (parallel to how this app already presents the 41-fold Kyrie), not as an abbreviation of missing text -- the full prayer text itself is given in full by O'Leary, nothing is omitted here.

title: Prayer of Abba Ephraem
text: O Lord, I have remembered thee now in this place. I believe, and pray thy Christliness do not give me into the hands of my enemies, that they may not boast themselves over thy servant nor gnash with their teeth upon me nor consume my unhappy life nor say "thou hast come into our hands and art delivered to us, this is the day we have expected". Do not forget me, O Lord, in thy mercy, and do not deal with me according to my sins nor turn thy face from me nor say to me "I know thee not". Thou, O Lord, through thy kindness didst draw me to thee; let not my enemies exult over me but extinguish their boastings and stop their works; and grant me, O Lord, thy mercy, that I may walk in thy way in innocence. And let my prayer come unto thee for I am not good, but for the sake of thy mercy and many kindnesses deliver my unhappy soul from death. And remember me, O Lord, for I have sinned and borne the condemnation of death. I cry to no physician save thee, nor to any other to loose my fetters; there is no God but thee. But I have fled to thy mercy, O Lord. O God of all things. Thou who dost give life by thy power, thou, O Lord, hast said, seek and ye shall find, ask and ye shall receive, knock and it shall be opened to you. Purge me, O Lord, from every sin that is to death, and do not reject my prayer, for I have turned myself to thee. For my heart is not pure, and my soul is unclean with sin. Hear me, O Lord, in thy mercy, for thou dost not reject the prayer of those who repent truly. But I have repented. Yet I am not clean, for I have repented at one hour and sinned the next hour. O strengthen me, Lord, in thy righteousness, set my feet upon the rock of repentance. Bestow goodness, O Lover of men, overcome those things which are within. As thou didst open the eyes of the blind, open the eyes of my dark heart: and as thou didst cleanse the leper by thy word, cleanse the impurities of my soul. Let thy mercy, O Lord, be as first in my inward parts, may it consume every polluting thought: for thou alone art merciful. O Light surpassing every light, O Joy surpassing every joy, O Rest exalted above all rest: thou art the true life, the power uncreated from eternity. And I pour out my soul before thee, O Merciful, and I pray thee that thou wilt forgive all my sins. For I am deserving of all punishment and torment: but I beseech thee do not forsake me, nor deliver me to my enemies, lest at any time they mock me in the desolation of my soul. Thou, O Lord, art pitiful and of loving-kindness, thou dost open thy heart to those who have sinned against thee. Raise up my songs, which sin has cast down in me. Revive my soul and mind which transgression has slain. Lighten the eyes of my heart which have been in darkness, that is the evil passion upon them. And deliver me from everything, for thine is the glory for ever and for all ages. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (16), pp. 115-116. Public domain. Given in full by O'Leary himself, no abbreviation to resolve.

title: The Sanctus
text: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord of Sabaoth. Heaven and earth are full of thy glory.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (17), p. 116. Public domain.

title: Concluding Doxology of the Midnight Office
text:
O thou begotten of the Father before all ages, Light of Light, Very God of Very God, Begotten, not created, Consubstantial with the Father, of whom is everything, and without whom was made nothing that was made: we thank thee, Lord Jesus Christ, and pray to thy goodness, O Lover of men. Through the intercessions of our Lady, the glory of our race, the Holy ever Virgin Mary, who was alone worthy to be thy mother in the latter times, and the prayers of our holy father the Evangelist Mark the Apostle, and the prayers of the Saints, have mercy upon us according to thy great mercy, and forgive all our sins and remove all our transgressions which have been and which are; and save us, protect us, and guard us against falls in our experiences. And may the grace of thy Holy Spirit the Paraclete renew the things that are within us, and strengthen us inwardly in this present and in the time that is to come.

Glory to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit; both now and ever, and unto the ages of ages. Amen.

May consolation come to us quickly, O Christ our God; grant it to thy servants, whilst our spirits are feeble within us. Cast not away our souls, nor leave our minds in tribulation, but come to us always and be near us, O thou who art everywhere; as thou wast with thy disciples always and didst teach them as they desired thee; guard us, O thou Merciful, so that we may praise thee perpetually and glorify thee for ever. Amen.

meta.source: O'Leary 1911, Midnight Office item (18), pp. 116-117. Public domain. 'Glory be, &c.' resolved to its full form per the no-placeholder governance rule.

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Sunday (Tone Adam)
text:
I have sought thee in the depth of my heart, O Lord Jesus help us.

Cast away from me the fetters of sin, O Lord Jesus help us.

Vouchsafe to me help and save me, O Lord Jesus help us.

May thy goodness establish me quickly, O Lord Jesus help us.

Shelter me under the shadow of thy wings, O Lord Jesus help us.

For in six days thou didst make all the universe, O Lord Jesus help us.

Seven times a day shall I praise thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

All creation glorifies thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

Thy dominion is established with thy power, O Lord Jesus help us.

Make haste my God to save me, O Lord Jesus help us.

Every knee bows in thy presence, O Lord Jesus help us.

Every tongue praises thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

Turn thy face away from my sins, O Lord Jesus help us.

Wipe out all our sins, O God; O Lord Jesus help us.

Thou who knowest my goings and searchest my reins, O Lord Jesus help us.

Create in me a clean heart, O Lord Jesus help us.

Take not thy Holy Spirit from me, O Lord Jesus help us.

Incline thy ear to me, hear me quickly, O Lord Jesus help us.

Strengthen to me thy law in the path of thy righteousness, O Lord Jesus help us.

Thy kingdom, O God, is an everlasting kingdom, O Lord Jesus help us.

Thou art the Son of God, I have believed in thee, O Lord Jesus help us.

Thou who takest away the sin of the world, have mercy on me, O Lord Jesus help us.

Purge me from the multitude of my sins, O Lord Jesus help us.

Every soul at once praises thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

Be patient with me, destroy me not quickly, O Lord Jesus help us.

When I arise at the first hour I will bless thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

Thy yoke is easy, thy burden is light, O Lord Jesus help us.

In an acceptable time hear me, O Lord Jesus help us.

As ointment poured forth is thy name, O Lord Jesus help us.

Drive from me every evil spirit, O Lord Jesus help us.

Plant within me the fruit of thy truth, O Lord Jesus help us.

Give us thy true peace, purge away our sins, O Lord Jesus help us.

Moreover when we assemble for prayer let us bless the name of the Lord Jesus. For I will bless thee, O Lord Jesus, and render thanks to thy name, for I have trusted in thee. So may we praise thee with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit, for thou didst rise and save us.

title: Alternative Psali for Sunday
text:
Come ye people, let us felicitate Mary the Virgin. Mary is a hope to us amongst the saints; mercy on us through her intercessions.

Gabriel the angel cried to her, "Hail Mary, pure dove." David cried and spoke of her glory, "O mountain of God, mountain full of glory."

Emmanuel our God took flesh in thee, O Mary, mother of God, source of our salvation.

Zacharias referred to thee as "daughter of Sion"; the King of Glory came and dwelt in thee.

Esaias said, "Behold a virgin shall bear a son, his name is Emmanuel." Rejoice in gladness, Mary the holy Virgin.

Ezekiel compared her, O ye orthodox, to a door closed fast towards the east. The Lord Jesus Christ has passed through it: he came and closed it in like manner again.

Every nation in the world gives glory to thee, O holy Mary. Mary the Virgin who was perfect, the holy Mother of God, the sacred Mary the Virgin.

All the patriarchs and prophets spoke to the glory of Mary the Virgin. Let every tree planted in all the earth salute the perfect fruit in the Holy Mary.

Further will I speak to the honour of the Virgin, the true Spouse, Mary the Queen. Thou, O Mary, art exalted above heaven, holy above the earth and all that is therein.

Be glad, O Virgin, rejoice in spirit, there is none like thee in all the earth.

Thou wast signified, Mother of God, Mary the Virgin, as the second tabernacle.

Blessed art thou amongst all women, for thou didst bear to us God, who came and saved us.

The Son of God, the Word, King of Ages, loved her beauty: he came and saved us. God who sits between the cherubim was desirous thereof.

Hail Mary with holy greeting; hail Virgin, Mother of our Saviour.

All psalmody that is uplifted, O ye orthodox, is befitting to her.

Blessed art thou above all women, for thou didst bear to us God, who came and saved us.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section I
text:
Thy righteousness is signified, O thou blessed amongst women, in that thou art the second tabernacle. It was she they referred to as the Holy of Holies wherein were the tables of the law, and the ten commandments which were written by the finger of God. That was symbolical to us of the Iota, the saving name of Jesus Christ. Who took flesh in her without essential change and became the mediator of a new covenant. Through the shedding of his holy blood he purged believers and justified a nation. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section I:

Who is able to relate the glory of the tabernacle which Moses made upon mount Sinai? He made it beautifully according to the word of the Lord, and according to all the types which were shown to him. Therein were Aaron and his sons ministering, in a type of the Most High and a symbol of heaven. They foreshadowed thee, Mary the Virgin, the true tabernacle wherein was God. Wherefore we exalt thee worthily in prophetic hymns, for they spoke honourable things of thee, the holy city of the great King. We pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section II
text:
The ark was covered with gold on every side, it was made of woods which do not decay. It was the symbol of God the Word, who became man, without separation. There is One from Two, undefiled Deity is undivided, consubstantial with the Father. And pure humanity without carnal intercourse, consubstantial with us according to nature. This which he took within her, the Holy One, imbued her as regards person. Wherefore every creature, exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section II:

At once every soul of the children of Israel brought gifts to the tabernacle of the Lord. Gold and silver and precious stones and fine linen and purple. They made an ark of woods which do not decay, they covered it with gold within and without. For thou, O Mary the Virgin, wast covered with the glory of the Deity within and without. That thou mightest bring many people to God the Son through thy purity. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section III
text:
The mercy-seat which covered it between the Cherubim was a type of God the Word who took flesh in thee, O spotless one, without essential change. He became the purger of sins and remover of iniquities. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section III:

The Cherubim were a symbol, they overshadowed the mercy-seat always with their wings. There was an overshadowing over the Holy of Holies in the second tabernacle. Over Mary also thousands of thousands, and ten thousand times ten thousand were overshadowing. They sang to their Creator placed in her womb, who took our form without sin by the change. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section IV
text:
Thou art the vessel of refined gold which was full of manna within. The bread of life which came down to us from heaven and gave life to the world. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section IV:

For the name is applied as suitable to thee, as the vessel of gold was full of manna. That was it which was placed in the tabernacle of witness of the children of Israel. On account of benefits which the Lord God decreed in a glorious manner at the desert of Sinai. Thou thyself Mary didst bear in thy womb the spiritual manna which came from the Father. Thou didst conceive him without stain; he gave us his body and his holy blood that we might live for ever. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section V
text:
Thou art the candlestick of pure gold which was for the ever filled lamp. He who gave light to the world was light from the Light unapproachable. Very God of Very God, who took flesh in her without essential change. Through his appearing he gave light to us who walked in darkness and the shadow of death. That he might guide our feet into the way of peace, through the communion of his holy mysteries. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section V:

Let every creature on high be incomparable to thee, O thou candlestick of gold which was for the true light. That which was there was made of gold which was chosen pure and was placed in the tabernacle. It was fashioned by the hands of men and intended for the lamp for day and night. He who was in the womb of Mary the Virgin enlightens every man who cometh into the world. For he is the sun of righteousness whom thou didst bear, he healed us from our sins. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section VI
text:
Thou art the censer of pure gold which was for the coal of burning fire. That it was he took from the altar that he might purge sins and remove our transgressions. That was God the Word who took flesh in her, he received it to be a sweet savour to God his Father. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section VI:

Then truly nothing was lacking, I understand of her that she was the golden censer. That which was therein was placed there for an excellent savour before the Holy of Holies. God used to remove the sins of the people through the sacrifice and odour of sweet savour. Thou indeed Mary didst bear in thy womb the incomprehensible Word of the Father. He offered up an acceptable sacrifice upon the cross for the salvation of our race. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section VII
text:
Hail Mary the pure dove who didst bear to us God the Word. Thou art the flower of sweet scent which blossomed forth on the root of Jesse. The rod of Aaron which blossomed without planting and watering was a type of thee. O thou who having borne Christ the Very God without seed of man didst remain a virgin. Wherefore every creature exalts her the Lady Mother of God the ever holy. We also pray that we may obtain mercy through her prayers to him the Lover of men.

Paraphrase of Section VII:

Thy righteousness is signified, O thou holy Mary, thou art the second tabernacle most holy. Therein was placed the rod of Aaron and the holy flower of sweet scent. Thou art clothed with purity without and within, O thou chaste tabernacle, abode of the righteous. The hosts on high and the choir of the just exalt thee with praises. Wherefore we exalt thee, worthily in prophetic hymns; we pray and beseech thee, may we obtain mercy through thy prayers to Him the Lover of men.

title: The Sunday Theotokia — Section VIII and Conclusion
text:
Thou art effectual above all the saints to pray for us, O thou full of grace. Thou art greatly exalted above the patriarchs and honoured above the prophets. Thy going forth is in splendour above the Cherubim and Seraphim. For thou art truly the praise of our race, and the advocate of our souls. Intercede with our Saviour for us, that he may confirm us in the saving faith. That he vouchsafe to us pardon of our sins, that we may obtain mercy through thy intercessions.

Conclusion:

Every creature on high, the thousands of angels and archangels, cannot attain the height of thy blessings, O thou who didst wear the glory of the Lord of Sabaoth. For thou didst send forth rays beyond the sun, thou art a light above the Cherubim, and the Seraphim with six wings overshadowed thee with gladness.

The glory of Mary is exalted above heaven; her praise is upon earth and those who dwell therein. For thou verily art the true way which is the road to highest heaven. Thou didst cause within thee joy and rejoicing; thou didst acquire might, O daughter of Sion. O thou who didst take upon thee the vesture of heaven that thou mightest clothe Adam with the garment of grace. Thou didst restore him to paradise, the place of joy and dwelling of the just.

A true tabernacle is Mary the Virgin, therein were placed the faithful witnesses. The undefiled ark covered with gold all over and the mercy-seat, and the cherubim were an image. The vase of gold filled with manna, that is the Word of the Father who took flesh in her. The candlestick of gold which was for the true light, that is the unapproachable Light of the world. The censer of gold which was for the coal of fire and the sweet savour of incense. The rod of Aaron which flowered with holy blossom and sweet smell. All these together signify to us the miraculous child-bearing of Mary the Virgin.

O Moses the Prophet, thou didst edify our souls by the splendour of the tabernacle which thou didst adorn. The first tabernacle which Moses made was a place for the cleansing of the sins of the children of Israel. He made it gloriously according to the word of the Lord and according to all the types which were shown to him. There was an ark placed in the tabernacle covered with gold within and without. There was a mercy-seat placed in the tabernacle, a cherubim of gold overshadowed it. There was a vase of gold placed in the tabernacle, it was filled with manna. There was a candlestick of gold placed in the tabernacle, upon it were seven lamps giving light. There was a censer of gold placed in the tabernacle, there was frankincense placed in its midst. There was a flower of sweet smell placed in the tabernacle, all the house of Israel did smell it. There was Aaron's rod placed in the tabernacle, it blossomed forth without planting and watering. There was a table of gold placed in the tabernacle, the shewbread was laid upon it. There was a High Priest placed in the tabernacle to offer sacrifices for the sins of the people. The Almighty smelled that and took away the sins of the people. Through Mary the daughter of Joachim we offer the true sacrifice for the purging of sins.

Who is able to relate the glory of the tabernacle which the prophet adorned. The precious writings of the Holy Scriptures were seen, they were greatly admired. They were considered with careful mind, they signified her in the holy writings. They meant Mary the daughter of Joachim, that she is the true tabernacle of the Lord of Sabaoth. They offered the ark on account of the Virgin, it was covered with gold on account of her virginity. They offered the mercy-seat on account of the Virgin, the cherubim of glory overshadowed it. They offered the vessel of gold on account of the Virgin, filled with manna on account of our Saviour. They offered the candlestick of gold on account of the Church, and its seven lamps on account of its seven hosts. They offered the censer of gold on account of the Virgin, its perfume on account of Emmanuel. They offered the sweet scented flower on account of Mary the Queen, therein was a sweet perfume on account of her virginity. They offered the rod of Aaron on account of the wood of the cross on which my Lord was crucified that he might save us. They offered the table of gold on account of the place of oblation, the shewbread on account of the Lord's body. They offered the High Priest on account of our Saviour the true sacrificer for the removal of sins. He who offered up an acceptable sacrifice upon the cross for the salvation of our race. His good Father sacrificed him upon Golgotha. He opened the gate of Paradise, he restored Adam as he was at first.

Through Mary the daughter of Joachim we know the sacrifice for the purging of sin. We ourselves pray that we may obtain mercy through thy intercessions to him the Lover of men.

title: Hymn on the Resurrection (Sunday)
text:
Who amongst the gods is like unto thee, O Lord? thou art the true God who doest wonders. Thou hast shown thy might amongst the nations, thou didst save thy people by thy arm. Thou didst descend to Hades and bring up the captives who were there. To us thou didst grant liberty, as a good God, for thou didst rise and save us.

Christ our God rose from the dead, he is the firstfruits of those who slept. He appeared to Mary Magdalene, he spoke to her and thus he said: "Go and announce to the brethren that they resort to Galilee, there shall they see me." Mary went to the Apostles; she said "I have seen the Lord", and the things he said to her.

Truly well did she in being solicitous, that holy Mary Magdalene. She went to the tomb on the first day of the week, she sought in haste the resurrection of the Lord. She saw the angel sitting upon the stone, he declared and said to her, "He is risen, he is not here." Wherefore we glorify him, we cry aloud and say, "Blessed be thou, Lord Jesus, for thou didst rise and save us."

title: Psali "Our Lord Jesus" for Monday (Tone Adam)
text:
Thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand sing and give praise to our Lord Jesus. Everything that says that the Lord is Jesus is a sword at hand to scatter the enemy. For thou truly art very greatly exalted beyond the heavens and above the earth. For all the just who are pleasing to God meditate in all thy law.

God is placed before them always, his holy name is always in their mouths.

Greatly exalted is thy kindness, thou doer of righteous things, O Lord Jesus.

God is Emmanuel, the true food, the tree of life, the deathless.

Collect within me all forms of speech that I may laud and glorify the Lord Jesus.

Jesus is our God, Jesus is our Lord, Jesus is the hope of Christians.

Little by little we reach thy remembrance and glorify thy name, O Lord Jesus.

Every distraction that exists may we lay aside, that we may purge our hearts with the name of the Lord Jesus.

May thy name, O Lord, be within us, that it may enlighten us in our inner man.

For who amongst the gods is like unto thee, O Lord? Thou art the true god who doest wonders.

Blessed art thou in truth, O Lord Jesus, with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit.

A sweet savour very greatly famous is thy holy name, O Lord Jesus.

O true lamb of God the Father, have mercy on us in thy kingdom.

For the mouth of thy Father which bears witness to thee that "thou art my son, to-day have I begotten thee".

They glorify thee, the cherubim and seraphim; they cannot look upon thee.

We behold thee, the lamb, upon the place of sacrifice; we take of thy body and thy sacred blood.

Every hymn which is in all the law, there is nothing else therein but similitudes of thee.

This is the true stone most precious, which the merchant sold his possessions and bought.

Bestow upon us now this stone, that it may illuminate us in the inner man.

Consolation of our souls, freshness of our hearts is thy holy name, O Lord Jesus.

O pitiful and merciful, of great pity, O Lord Jesus.

The cherubim wave their wings; they sing and give praise, O Lord Jesus.

The sun will set and the moon in time; but thou, thou art, thy years do not fail.

In the providence of thy goodness thou dost bend the heavens, thou dost descend upon us.

As the true physician who gives healing thou dost cure all our diseases.

Look upon me, O Lord Jesus, with the pitying eye of thy goodness.

Plant within us an upright heart that we may bless thee, O Lord Jesus.

I pray to thee, Lord Jesus, have mercy on us in thy kingdom.

Moreover when we may give ourselves to prayer, let us bless the name of the Lord Jesus. For I will praise thee, O Lord Jesus, through thy name, for I have trusted in thee. Let us laud thee with thy good Father and the Holy Spirit, for thou didst rise and save us.
